topic_tag: an eighteenth-century map of a kingdom
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps showed the kingdom's roads and towns as they stood. The surveyor also drew, in dotted lines, a canal between the kingdom's two great rivers and roads to three hill villages with fast streams. The canal opened in 1840 links the same two river towns his dotted line linked, and by 1860 those three villages had become the kingdom's chief mill towns. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: The map drew a canal and village roads that did not yet exist, and decades later the canal joined the same towns and the villages grew into mill towns, so the map was "prescient." "Provincial" fails because the map looked across the whole kingdom, joining its two great rivers. "Portable" fails because nothing is said about the map's size or how it was carried. "Rigorous" fails because what set the map apart was what it foresaw, not the care of its measurements.

provincial.quote: a canal between the kingdom's two great rivers
provincial.why: the map's distinctive features span the whole kingdom, not one home district

portable.why: what distinguished the map was what it drew, not its physical form

rigorous.quote: showed the kingdom's roads and towns as they stood
rigorous.why: the rivals recorded what existed; the surveyor's difference was drawing what did not yet exist, not measuring more carefully

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps gave each county space in proportion to its size. The surveyor's home county, one of the smallest, filled nearly half his sheet, down to its lanes, mills and ferries, while the rest of the kingdom shared the other half with only its largest towns marked, and nearly every printing was sold in that county's market towns. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: A map of the whole kingdom gave half its space to one small home county and was bought almost entirely there, so it was "provincial," centered on local concerns. "Prescient" fails because the map recorded what existed rather than anticipating anything. "Portable" fails because the passage describes the map's layout, not its size or form. "Rigorous" fails because the map shows most of the kingdom only in outline, with its largest towns.

prescient.quote: down to its lanes, mills and ferries
prescient.why: the map detailed things already there, foreseeing nothing

portable.why: the passage concerns how space on the sheet was divided, not whether the map could be carried

rigorous.quote: with only its largest towns marked
rigorous.why: most of the kingdom was sketched thinly, the opposite of careful, thorough coverage

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps were engraved on sheets a yard wide, meant to hang in a study or lie open on a library table. The surveyor printed his on linen cut into sixteen panels, and the copies that survive, most of them owned by cattle drovers and traveling merchants, are worn through in a grid of creases. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: Unlike wall and table maps, the surveyor's linen map in panels was owned by drovers and merchants and worn through along its creases from being folded and carried, so it was "portable." "Prescient" fails because nothing is said about the map anticipating later events. "Provincial" fails because it was used by people traveling the kingdom, and nothing suggests it favored one district. "Rigorous" fails because the passage describes the map's form and use, not the accuracy of its survey.

prescient.quote: printed his on linen cut into sixteen panels
prescient.why: the map's distinction lay in its material and form, not in foreseeing anything

provincial.why: its users traveled the kingdom with it, giving no sign of a narrowly local outlook

rigorous.quote: worn through in a grid of creases
rigorous.why: the evidence concerns how the map was handled, not how carefully it was measured

worlds.passage: In 1790 a country surveyor published a map of the kingdom that went through eleven printings in twenty years. Rival maps copied their coastlines and roads from older charts, errors and all. The surveyor spent eleven summers on the kingdom's roads with a chain and a brass quadrant, plotting each town himself. When the government checked his sheets with better instruments sixty years later, few of his distances were off by more than a mile. Comparing it with other maps of its day, one historian describes the surveyor's map as, above all, ______.
worlds.explanation: Where rivals copied old errors, the surveyor spent eleven summers measuring roads and plotting towns himself, and a later survey found his distances nearly exact, so the map was "rigorous." "Prescient" fails because the map recorded what existed accurately rather than anticipating what would come. "Provincial" fails because his measurements covered the whole kingdom. "Portable" fails because nothing is said about the map's size or how it was carried.

prescient.quote: few of his distances were off
prescient.why: the later check confirms the accuracy of distances that already existed, not a prediction

provincial.quote: eleven summers on the kingdom's roads
provincial.why: the survey covered the kingdom's roads, not one home district

portable.quote: with a chain and a brass quadrant
portable.why: the passage concerns how the map was made accurate, not its physical form
